newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gilts capped by 114-31 before budget.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gilts capped by 114-31 before budget.

text.p: September gilt futures on LIFFE will be hard pressed to make much headway before the looming budget, technical analysts said on Monday.
They will find layers of resistance at 114-19 and 114-31 difficult to penetrate before the budget on Wednesday.
"Volatility is going to get less and less this week," Marc Ostwald, technical strategist at London Bond Broking, said. "They have a wait and see attitude with a slight upside bias."
Gilts were quoted at 114-17, up 2/32 at 0734 GMT.
Initial resistance would come from the highs of 114-19 on Friday and 114-18 on June 17, Ostwald said.
Beyond initial resistance, the contract high at 114-31 loomed, he said. "I don't think we can get beyond that."
Ostwald said support this session surfaced at the highs from June 25 and June 26 at 114-04 and 114-02.
"If there was some appalling news out we could actually get back through to 113-22,25 but I just don't think there's going to be very much volatility," he said.
UK June money supply data and May consumer credit data will be released at 0830 GMT.
Technical analysts at the Royal Bank of Scotland were optimistic.
"The long-term timing analysis indicates that the continuation chart high at 114-24 recorded on May 9 should be bypassed this week," Juliette Clark of RBS said in a note.
She said the next Gann objective was at 115-21/23.
"In the shorter term though, the hourly momentums have soared into overbought ground and this may limit the initial upward potential," she said.
If the contract was unable to get past the 114-23/24 barrier it would likely consolidate at current levels, she added.
At the short end, December short sterling was quoted at 92.78, unchanged on the day.
